bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ {*} Crash State: rpl_glob read_config_expand read_config_expand Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.normalized: Wget2 reads the staged fuzz file as a config file, parses its single record as an `include` directive, and recursively calls `glob(..., GLOB_TILDE)` on an attacker-controlled path beginning `~lp/` and containing a second `/` later in the same string. In gnulib's `rpl_glob`, the specific-user tilde-expansion path computes `end_name` as a pointer into the heap `dirname` buffer, then frees `dirname` before copying the `end_name` suffix into the rebuilt path. The later `mempcpy(d, end_name, rest_len)` therefore reads from freed heap memory, producing the observed heap-use-after-free.

source.description: Reads the attacker-controlled config record from the staged `--config` file into `buf` for option parsing.
source.value_from: The fuzz harness exposes the staged `poc` bytes as the contents of the config file `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8428e` via `fmemopen((void *) g_data, g_size, "r")`, and `read_config_expand()` reads that file here. The observed witness is a single 122-byte line that begins `include@~lp/`.
source.note: This read happens in the `expand == 0` fallback after the initial `glob("d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8428e", ...)` no-match path. The line read here is later parsed as an `include` statement whose value begins `~lp/`.

root_cause.description: The specific-user tilde-expansion branch frees `dirname` even though `end_name` still aliases inside that heap buffer.
root_cause.note: For the crashing path, `end_name` points 3 bytes into the 48-byte `dirname` allocation and `rest_len` is 44. The fix commit delays this free until after the later `mempcpy(d, end_name, rest_len)` so the alias stays valid while it is still being used.

sink.description: Copies bytes from the stale `end_name` alias after `dirname` has already been freed.
sink.note: ASAN reports a `READ of size 44` here at an address 3 bytes inside the 48-byte region allocated at line 565 and freed at line 849. The stale source pointer is `end_name`, not the new destination buffer.

parser_admitted.description: The config record is admitted as an `include` statement, so the parsed attacker-controlled value beginning `~lp/` is forwarded to recursive config expansion and then into `glob(..., GLOB_TILDE)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Harness wrapper exposes the fuzzer buffer as the contents of the config file named `d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8428e`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput stores the raw `data,size` pair into `g_data` and `g_size` at lines 101-102 before `init()` opens the staged `--config` file.
tainted_value_origin.note: When `options.c` later opens that filename in read mode, it receives a `FILE *` backed directly by the staged `poc` bytes.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz harness maps the staged `poc` bytes onto the requested `--config` file name so Wget2 reads the input as a config file.
Wget2 reads the attacker-controlled config line, parses it as an `include` statement, and recursively calls `glob()` with `GLOB_TILDE` on the parsed include path.
The specific-user tilde-expansion path derives `end_name` as an alias into heap `dirname`, frees `dirname`, and then `mempcpy()` reads 44 bytes from that stale alias.

fine_trace.note: Reads one record from the attacker-controlled config file into `buf`. In the saved witness the full 122-byte file is one line beginning `include@~lp/`, so the later parser sees the entire PoC as a single config record.

Parses the record as a statement. Because the first non-name byte is `@`, `parse_option()` terminates `name` as `"include"` and sets `val` to the remaining bytes, which start with `~lp/` and still contain a later `/` before the first NUL.
Because the parsed statement name is `include`, Wget2 recursively processes the attacker-controlled `val` with expansion enabled.
The recursive include path is passed to `glob()` with `GLOB_TILDE`, so the string beginning `~lp/` enters gnulib's tilde-expansion logic instead of being treated as a literal pathname.

Inside `rpl_glob`, `strrchr(pattern, '/')` selects the last slash in the attacker path. The 47-byte prefix before that slash is heap-allocated and copied into `dirname`, producing the same 48-byte region ASAN reports as the later freed allocation.

The specific-user tilde branch runs because `dirname` starts with `~lp`. `end_name` is set to the first slash inside `dirname`, so it aliases 3 bytes into the heap buffer at the start of the `/...` suffix that will later be copied.

The username taken from `dirname + 1` up to `end_name - 1` is `"lp"`. On the saved crashing run `getpwnam_r()` resolves that user, so execution enters the branch that rebuilds `dirname` from `p->pw_dir`.
Computes the length of the aliased suffix that will be copied later. For the staged witness `rest_len` is 44, which matches ASAN's `READ of size 44` at the sink.
Frees the heap `dirname` buffer while `end_name` still points inside it. This is the lifetime break fixed by the patch, which saves the old pointer and delays the free until after the suffix copy.

Copies 44 bytes from the stale `end_name` pointer into the rebuilt path buffer after `dirname` has already been freed. ASAN reports the resulting heap-use-after-free read at an address 3 bytes inside the freed 48-byte region.

allocation_context.note: ASAN reports the freed region as a 48-byte heap allocation made at this `malloc(dirlen + 1)` site.

free_context.note: ASAN reports the same region freed here before the later `mempcpy()` read at line 868.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `reproduction_report.json`, `patch.diff`, staged vulnerable source under `_work/src/wget2`, and the saved `poc`; Stage 02 did not rerun vulnerable or fixed binaries

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run fed the staged `poc` to `/out/wget_options_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free` with stack `rpl_glob -> read_config_expand -> read_config_expand`.

format.name: Wget2 config file record
format.contract: Exactly the staged 122-byte witness in `poc` (sha256 `dba78e23d740124510064e053835174384fa0c0450d5d8a06dcc2087eb163c8e`). When read as the `--config` file, it is a single record that begins `include@~lp/` and still contains a later `/` before the first NUL byte. `parse_option()` therefore yields the statement name `include` and an include-path value beginning `~lp/...`; the recursive `glob(..., GLOB_TILDE)` call takes gnulib's specific-user tilde branch, allocates the 47-byte prefix before the final slash as `dirname`, sets `end_name` to the first slash inside that heap buffer, and later performs the saved 44-byte UAF read when `mempcpy(d, end_name, rest_len)` runs after `free(dirname)`. This contract is limited to the staged witness and the observed crashing environment, where the parsed username `lp` resolved to a passwd entry; it does not claim every `include ~user/.../suffix` record will reproduce.
